title: Projection formula for proper morphisms
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
proper morphism and
$\Lambda$ a torsion ring. For $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and
$K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the canonical projection-formula morphism

$$
\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K):\quad
Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K\longrightarrow
Rf_*(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K)
$$

of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For a geometric point $g:s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, form $X_s=X\times_Ys$ with projections $f_s$ and $g'$. Properness is stable under base change, so $X_s$ is proper over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, hence separated and of finite type over $\Omega$; Finite type over the affine point gives quasi-compactness. Its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse image of an affine open is a closed affine subscheme and is quasi-compact; thus it is quasi-separated. Clause (2) of [lem-kun-0f10] therefore gives $\operatorname{cd}(X_s)<\infty$. Here finiteness is used only on the geometric fiber, not asserted for an arbitrary base $Y$.

Put $E_s=g'^{-1}E$ and $M=K_{\bar y}$. By [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], $g^{-1}K$ is the stalk complex $M$. Over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ the Galois group is trivial, so [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] identifies abelian sheaves on $s$ with abelian groups. This identification carries a $\Lambda$-action to its endomorphisms on the group, with the same ring identities, and conversely carries these endomorphisms back by full faithfulness. It thus identifies $\Lambda$-module sheaves with $\Lambda$-modules. This additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels, hence is exact; applying it termwise preserves and reflects quasi-isomorphisms, so it induces the same identification on unbounded derived categories. Consequently $f_s^{-1}g^{-1}K$ is the constant complex $\underline M$.

Apply [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] to $E$ and to $E\otimes^L_\Lambda f^{-1}K$. These are arbitrary unbounded $\Lambda$-complexes, as allowed by that lemma. Its two exchange maps are isomorphisms. Monoidality [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] identifies the pulled-back tensor product with $E_s\otimes^L_\Lambda f_s^{-1}g^{-1}K$. The commuting square of [lem-kun-proj-formula-natural] then identifies $g^{-1}\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K)$, through these isomorphisms, with $\mathrm{PF}_{f_s}(E_s,M)$. This is the canonical map, not merely an abstract isomorphism of its source and target.

Since $X_s$ is qcqs of finite cohomological dimension by Step 1 and $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring, [lem-kun-0f12] applied to $E_s$ and $M\in D(\Lambda)$ makes the canonical map $R\Gamma(X_s,E_s)\otimes^L_\Lambda M\to R\Gamma(X_s,E_s\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline M)$ an isomorphism. Under Step 2 this is exactly the fiber projection map, by its adjoint definition [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Step 3 therefore shows that the original map is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk.

For every integer $i$, exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies the stalk of $\mathcal H^i(\mathrm{PF}_f)$ with the cohomology in degree $i$ of the stalk map, hence with an isomorphism by Step 4. Forgetting the $\Lambda$-action does not change kernels or cokernels. Sheaf stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes every $\mathcal H^i(\mathrm{PF}_f)$ an isomorphism. Its cone is therefore acyclic, which is precisely invertibility in the derived category. This argument does not require a bound on either complex.
